summary: This document outlines the requirements for building a CLI-based personal wiki using a local open-weight Gemma model and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Students must implement a harness that supports three distinct modes: chat, ask, and search, ensuring the entire system functions offline.
key_facts: Build a CLI and harness to interact with local data using a local open-weight Gemma model.
Implement three required modes: Chat (personal assistant), Ask (factual research), and Search (inspect original sources).
The system must function entirely offline for the final demonstration.
The project requires a personal wiki in Obsidian with at least three original sources and linked pages.
Students must provide evidence of four ask-mode tests: three answerable questions and one question with insufficient evidence.
The README must include device specs, model/version, quantization, and measured memory use and response time.
The harness must manage conversation context, tool calls, prompt assembly, and citation checks.
The project is graded on deliverable quality, testing & evaluation, and working results.

concepts.name: RAG
concepts.definition: A workflow where relevant passages are retrieved and included in a prompt to provide context for a model's answer.
concepts.in_this_source: The document defines the RAG workflow as retrieving relevant passages and including them in a prompt for the model to answer using that evidence.

tools.name: Gemma
tools.definition: An open-weight large language model developed by Google.
tools.in_this_source: The project requires using a local, quantized version of the Gemma model to generate text and organize linked pages.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.definition: A knowledge management and note-taking application.
tools.in_this_source: The project requires using Obsidian to view the generated wiki, including its page list, index, and graph view.
